inputs.cash_note: Cash, cash equivalents and investments at 2026-06-30 per Q2-26 10-Q balance sheet: cash 2,760.4 + current marketable securities 2,455.8 + non-current marketable securities 3,409.3 = 8,625.5. Investment-grade debt securities are counted as cash because the interest they earn is stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule). No borrowings of any kind.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: share-based compensation expense 802.8 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense; cash-flow add-back is 788.2) + taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards 419.1 (financing activities). ISRG publishes no combined SBC-plus-award-tax figure, so the two lines are summed per house method. Proceeds from stock plans (ESPP/option exercises, 350.3 in FY2025) are NOT netted against the charge.
inputs.interest_income_source: FY2025 10-K 'Interest and other income, net' (NonoperatingIncomeExpense) 365.9; TTM to Q2-26 is 354.6. The line is almost entirely interest on the ~$8.6-9.0bn cash-and-investments pile (implied yield ~4%), which is added back at the end of the DCF, so it is stripped from the FCF base to avoid counting the pile twice.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 2,295.3 (cash, financing activities); H1-2026 a further 1,443.5. Diluted count has fallen 364.4 -> 357.3 over the twelve months to Q2-26. ISRG is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded rather than a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares for Q2 2026 (357.3m, 10-Q filed 2026-07-21); period-end basic was 353.9m. Held FLAT because SBC (including award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close per Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketTime); not an after-hours print. 52-week range 328.57-603.88.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP ~5%, equity beta ~1.0-1.2 for a large-cap no-debt medtech gives a cost of equity of 9-10%; with zero debt WACC = cost of equity. 9.0% used, held identical across all three scenarios so that risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not twice through a per-scenario rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating leases (liability $171m at FY2025, immaterial against $8.6bn of cash) stay inside operating expenses/EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Systems ISRG places with customers under operating leases are ISRG's own PP&E funded through inventory (an OCF working-capital outflow), which is why the working-capital capture is strongly negative.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows include the Intuitive-Fosun China JV; NCI earned 20.6 of FY2025 net income (book NCI 129.3 at 2026-06-30). Deducted once, in the equity bridge, at ~15x NCI earnings (310) rather than at book, so the flows stay consolidated and the minority is charged at a market-like value.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: US operating company). Reason: ISRG is a single-segment razor/razor-blade operating business (instruments and accessories ~60% of revenue, systems ~24%, service ~16%) with no debt, positive and growing free cash flow, and no fair-value, deposit or AFFO complications; none of the non-FCF routes apply and none of the owner-fcf-adaptations (non-USD, leases, NCI beyond a small JV, SBC-zero) are material. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); H1-2026 actuals (revenue +20.7%, GAAP operating margin 32.3%) and the July-2026 FY2026 outlook (da Vinci procedures +13.5-15.5%, closer to midpoint; non-GAAP gross margin 68-69% including a 1.0%-of-revenue tariff hit; non-GAAP opex +11-13%) anchor year 1. Owner FCF FY2025 = 2,490.7 - 1,221.9 - 365.9 = 902.9 (9.0% of revenue) versus a 24.7% reported FCF margin: the gap is SBC 8.0%, net-share-settlement taxes 4.2% and interest income 3.6% of revenue. FY2023-24 owner FCF was ~zero/negative during the facilities capex supercycle (capex 1,064 and 1,111), so the owner-FCF CAGRs are not a usable growth anchor; the revenue CAGR and guidance are. 10-year horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping (15% year 1 -> ~25% mature) as SBC% declines and the working-capital drag shrinks with growth. Working capital: FY2024-25 OCF ran ~900-1,150 below NI+D&A+SBC on revenue increases of 1,228 and 1,713 (lease-fleet build via inventory, receivables, inventory) -> capture ~ -65/-75%; H1-26 ran ~ -44%. -50% used on the CHANGE in revenue, so the drag fades as growth decelerates. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes 537.9 = 21% of engine EBIT; GAAP ETR 13% is flattered by excess tax benefits on SBC that are not perpetuated, so the path ramps 20% -> 22% (ISRG's own non-GAAP ETR guidance is ~22-23%). No filing text is extracted for this ticker (US XBRL route); component lines were read from the SEC companyfacts API and the Q2-26 8-K EX-99.1.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest (Intuitive-Fosun JV) at ~15x FY2025 NCI earnings
equity_bridge.note: NCI earned 20.6 in FY2025; book NCI 129.3 at 2026-06-30 (Q2-26 10-Q). Charged once here; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.9% vs revenue 5yr 18.2% (-29%) and EPS 5yr 21.5% (-40%): equity growth is depressed by $4.6bn of buybacks in FY2022 and FY2025, so book value understates the compounding rate. Year-1 growth in the scenarios is anchored to FY2026 guidance and H1-26 actuals, not to this figure; the 12.9% is the forward proxy for screening only.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) on the Metrics CSV. Owner-FCF CAGRs use the SBC-, award-tax- and interest-adjusted series above, which was ~zero in FY2023-24 during the facilities capex supercycle (capex 1,064 and 1,111 vs 540 in FY2025); the 60.6% 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is off a trough and is not a usable anchor. SBC+award taxes grew 26%/yr FY2020-25 (574 -> 1,222) against reported FCF growth of 17%: an increasing share of reported cash growth is being paid for in stock and withholding cash.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 17.5%: H1-26 revenue +20.7%; procedures guided +13.5-15.5% (nearer midpoint) with systems/lease revenue and da Vinci 5 pricing running ahead of procedures; H2 comps harden (Q4-25 was 2,866). Decelerates ~1.5pp/yr toward 5% by year 10, averaging ~10% -- below the 15.5% 10-year and 18% 5-year revenue CAGRs, reflecting ~3.2m procedures against a mid-teens-million addressable pool, US general-surgery penetration still low, and competitive entry (Hugo, Ottava) capping the later years.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-D&A) was 43.3% in FY2025 and ~46% in H1-26. Guidance of 68-69% non-GAAP gross margin (after a 1% tariff hit) with opex growing 11-13% against ~17% revenue implies 1.5-2pp of leverage in FY2026; thereafter +0.5pp/yr to 48% mature as da Vinci 5 mix and service scale offset tariffs and China pricing.
base.sbc_rationale: Anchor 11.5% (FY2025 12.1%, TTM 11.2%); SBC expense alone is a stable ~8% of revenue, the withholding-tax component is what varies with the share price. Declines ~0.4pp/yr to 8% mature.
base.wc_rationale: -50% of the change in revenue: FY2024-25 ran -65/-75% (lease-fleet build via inventory, receivables, inventory), H1-26 ~ -44%. Modelled on growth so the drag fades as growth decelerates.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes 537.9 in FY2025 = ~21% of engine EBIT. GAAP ETR 13% is flattered by excess SBC tax benefits that are not perpetuated; ramps to 22% (ISRG non-GAAP ETR guidance ~22-23%).

scenario_narratives.base: Da Vinci procedure growth runs at the guided ~14.5% in 2026 and decelerates gradually as US general-surgery penetration deepens, international (Europe, Japan, India) expands and da Vinci 5 replaces the Xi fleet; systems revenue tracks procedures via the usage-based lease model. Gross margin holds 68-69% after a ~1% tariff drag, opex grows slower than revenue, and adjusted EBITDA reaches ~48% by 2030. SBC stays a significant recurring expense (~8% of revenue) with net-share-settlement taxes fading as a share of revenue. Competition from Medtronic Hugo (US clearance 2025) and J&J Ottava takes share at the margin in the late 2020s, which is what brings growth to 5% by 2035. The working-capital drag from building the leased fleet shrinks as growth slows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Ion and SP add second and third growth legs, da Vinci 5 force-feedback and digital tools widen the clinical-evidence moat, and procedure growth holds mid-teens through 2028 before decelerating. Pricing on da Vinci 5, service scale and manufacturing regionalisation lift adjusted EBITDA to ~51%, and SBC declines to ~7% of revenue as the employee base matures. Competitors remain sub-scale in soft-tissue surgery and hospital capex favours the incumbent's installed base (11,710 systems at Q2-26). Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hugo and Ottava reach commercial scale in the US and Europe by 2028 and hospitals use them as pricing leverage; China volume-based procurement and domestic robots (MicroPort MedBot, Edge) cap Asia pricing; tariffs persist or widen beyond the 1% of revenue guided; and reimbursement pressure on elective procedures slows the shift to robotics. Procedure growth falls to mid-single digits by 2029, adjusted EBITDA erodes to 42% as pricing softens and R&D must be sustained, SBC stays near 10% of revenue, and the lease-fleet capital intensity does not fade. Terminal growth 2.5%. The balance sheet ($8.6bn cash, no debt) means this is a value-compression case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 20/50/30. Bear up because credible competitors are now cleared in the US (Hugo) with Ottava following, tariff exposure is explicit in guidance, and the valuation's duration (terminal value ~70% of EV) makes late-decade share loss unusually costly; still well short of the 25-35% reserved for solvency or single-regulator risk because ISRG carries no debt and $8.6bn of cash. Bull trimmed because it needs three independent things -- mid-teens procedure growth held to 2028, EBITDA expansion to 51% while competition arrives, and SBC compression to 7% -- to hold at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House-basis owner-FCF DCF: SBC and net-share-settlement taxes are charged as cash costs, interest on the cash pile is stripped and the pile added back once, the share count is held flat, and the FCF margin is built from components so the FY2025 working-capital and capex troughs are neither perpetuated nor ignored. The street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside so the reader can see how much of the market price depends on that accounting choice.
key_risks_to_valuation: Competitive entry: Medtronic Hugo (US) and J&J Ottava reaching scale would pressure system pricing and slow procedure share gains -- the bear axis.
Tariffs: guidance embeds ~1% of revenue; a broader regime on components or finished systems would compress gross margin further.
China: volume-based procurement and domestic robots cap pricing in the fastest-growing region; the Fosun JV NCI is small but the market exposure is not.
SBC treatment: house and street values differ materially because SBC plus award taxes run ~12% of revenue; the market price sits inside that band.
Terminal-value dominance: a 10-year build with margins still maturing leaves ~70% of value in the terminal; each 1pp of WACC moves value by roughly a fifth (see sensitivity grid).

Working-capital capture (-50% of revenue change) is the least-observed driver: the leased-fleet build sits in OCF as inventory, and if leasing mix keeps rising the drag could persist longer than modelled.
